# Engine Simulator 2.0

Engine simulator for ECU testing based on the Speeduino V0.4 and the ESP32-32U DevKitC.

The system connects to the ECU through the standard Speeduino 40-pin IDC connector and generates signals to simulate real engine operation.

## Architecture

### Signals generated by the ESP32

| Signal | ESP32 Pin | To Speeduino | Method |
|:-------|:---------:|:-------------:|:-------|
| Crank Trigger | GPIO 12 | IDC Pin 25 | Square wave via hardware timer and 3.3V-to-5V level shifter |
| Cam 1 Trigger | GPIO 13 | IDC Pin 24 | Square wave via hardware timer and 3.3V-to-5V level shifter |
| Cam 2 Trigger | GPIO 14 | IDC Pin 24 (optional) | Square wave via hardware timer and 3.3V-to-5V level shifter |
| CLT (Coolant Temperature) | GPIO 26 (DAC2) | IDC Pin 19 | Analog voltage 0–3.3V, amplified to 0–5V |
| MAP (Pressure) | GPIO 25 (DAC1) | IDC Pin 11 | Analog voltage 0–3.3V, amplified to 0–5V |

### Manually controlled signals (potentiometers)

| Signal | Speeduino Pin | Notes |
|:--------|:-------------:|:------|
| TPS (Throttle Position Sensor) | IDC Pin 22 | 5V potentiometer, wiper/common connected to ESP32 ADC (GPIO 34) through a voltage divider |
| IAT (Intake Air Temperature) | IDC Pin 20 | Potentiometer connected directly to Speeduino |
| O2 (Oxygen Sensor) | IDC Pin 21 | Potentiometer connected directly to Speeduino |

### ECU input signals

| Signal | ESP32 Pin | From Speeduino | Notes |
|:-------|:---------:|:--------------:|:------|
| Fan Feedback | GPIO 27 | IDC Pin 15 | Fan status (0V = ON), 5V-to-3.3V voltage divider |

### ECU outputs monitoring

Speeduino outputs such as injectors, ignition/coils, fan, idle, VVT, boost, and fuel pump are read by the ESP32 through CD4050BE buffers for timing calculation (Phase 2).

---

## Firmware features

- 64 trigger wheel / crank patterns (ArduStim compatible): 60-2, 36-1, 24-1, LS1, 58X, Chrysler NGC, BMW N20, GM 40-tooth OSS, and many others
- RPM inertia model: cranking from 0 to 350 RPM, then idle at 850 RPM + (TPS × 6150), with low-pass filtering
- Start/Stop button: starts and stops the engine with a cranking ramp, idle stabilization, and gradual shutdown
- Dynamic MAP simulation: 100 kPa with engine off, 85 kPa during cranking, and 30–100 kPa depending on RPM and TPS
- Dynamic CLT simulation: gradual warm-up, fan cooling, and Newton cooling when engine is off
- USB serial interface: ArduStim protocol for configuring trigger wheel and crank pattern, as well as RPM mode from TunerStudio
- Speeduino timing monitoring (Phase 2): input capture via ISR on 9 CD4050BE inputs (4 injectors + 4 coils + fan), measuring injector on-time, pulse frequency, duty cycle, ignition dwell and advance
- WiFi AP + web dashboard (Phase 3): SSID `EngineSimulator2.0`, password `1234567890`, IP `192.168.254.1`, responsive dashboard at `/`, allows selecting one of 64 trigger patterns and persists the setting to NVS memory

### Verification status

| Module | Status |
|:-------|:-------|
| Phase 1 — Crank/Cam generation and engine model | Verified on hardware (Speeduino / Mega2560 reads engine speed correctly; fixed GPIO register usage `GPIO.out_w1ts/w1tc` in the ISR for core v3.3.x) |
| Phase 2 — Injector/ignition timing (input capture) | Implemented and compiled successfully — hardware validation pending |
| Phase 3 — WiFi AP + web dashboard | Implemented and compiled successfully — hardware validation pending |

## Hardware requirements

### Main components

| Component | Quantity | Description |
|:-----------|:---------:|:------------|
| ESP32-WROOM-32U | 1 | Main microcontroller |
| 74AHCT125 | 1 | Quadruple level shifter 3.3V -> 5V (Crank, Cam1, Cam2) |
| TLV2372 | 1 | Dual rail-to-rail op-amp (MAP/CLT buffers) |
| R-78E5.0-1.0 (RECOM) | 1 | Switching regulator drop-in 12V -> 5V, 1A, 91% efficiency |
| 40-pin IDC connector | 1 | Connection to Speeduino V0.4 |
| CD4050BE | 2 | Hex buffer for ECU inputs (injectors, ignition, fan) |
| Trimmer potentiometers | 5 | (2 kΩ x2, 10 kΩ x3) — TPS, IAT, O2, and others |
| Push button | 1 | Start/Stop |
| DC barrel jack | 1 | 12V power input |

### Voltage levels

| Section | Voltage | Method |
|:---------|:--------:|:-------|
| Board power supply | 12V | External DC barrel jack |
| Logic supply | 5V | R-78E5.0-1.0 switching regulator from 12V |
| ESP32 and sensors | 3.3V | Onboard regulator |
| ESP32 digital outputs -> ECU | 3.3V -> 5V | 74AHCT125 |
| ESP32 analog outputs -> ECU | 0–3.3V -> 0–5V | TLV2372 (gain 1.5x) |
| Fan input from ECU | 5V -> 3.3V | Resistive divider |

## Build and upload

### Prerequisites

- [Arduino IDE](https://www.arduino.cc/en/software) or [Arduino CLI](https://arduino.github.io/arduino-cli/)
- ESP32 board package installed: `esp32:esp32` via Board Manager
- Selected board: `ESP32 Dev Module` or `ESP32-WROOM-32U`
- Libraries for the dashboard (Phase 3): use **ESP32Async** (compatible with ESP32 core v3.3.x and mbedTLS 3; the classic `me-no-dev` version does not compile)
  - **ESP Async WebServer** (`arduino-cli lib install "ESP Async WebServer"`)
  - **Async TCP** (`arduino-cli lib install "Async TCP"`)

### Compile and upload

```bash
# Via Arduino CLI (first time: install the dashboard libraries as well)
arduino-cli lib install "ESP Async WebServer" "Async TCP"
arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32 firmware/Engine_Simulator_2.0.ino
arduino-cli upload --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32 --port COMx firmware/Engine_Simulator_2.0.ino
```

### Configuration

The trigger wheel/crank pattern can be selected in the following ways:

1. Dashboard web interface (recommended): connect to WiFi `EngineSimulator2.0` (password `1234567890`) and open `http://192.168.254.1` -> page `/setup` to select the pattern (persisted to NVS memory)
2. USB serial (115200 baud): use command `X` to select the next pattern, or `S<n>` to select by index
3. ArduStim GUI: desktop software connecting via serial to configure patterns and modes

## Project notes

- The integrated MAP sensor on the Speeduino V0.4 (IDC Pin 11) cannot be used as an alternative to the DAC-generated signal from the ESP32 for simulation. In this case, the MAP pin of the IDC must be disconnected and re-routed to the proper simulation output.
- The fan is managed with feedback: Speeduino controls it, and the ESP32 reads it to model CLT temperature.
- The IAT and O2 potentiometers are purely manual and do not affect the ESP32 simulation. They are used to test ECU corrections.
- The KiCad PCB (`Hardware/Engine Simulator 2.0/`) is complete: 2-layer routing with a solid GND plane on the bottom copper layer and thermal reliefs. DRC: no clearance errors and no unconnected pads; only cosmetic warnings remain.
- The design is intended to be a compact, low-cost and fully functional engine simulation interface for ECU testing and development.

### Manufacturing outputs (Gerber + drill)

Manufacturing files are generated with `kicad-cli` and are ready for any fabrication house (JLCPCB, PCBWay, PCBcart):

- `Hardware/Engine Simulator 2.0/Gerbers/` — Gerber RS-274X, 9 layers (`F_Cu`, `B_Cu`, `F_Paste`, `B_Paste`, `F_Mask`, `B_Mask`, `F_SilkS`, `B_SilkS`, `Edge_Cuts`) + `.gbrjob` file
- `Hardware/Engine Simulator 2.0/Gerbers/` — Separate Excellon drill files: `-PTH.drl` (plated holes, 0.3–2.2 mm) and `-NPTH.drl` (non-plated holes)
- `Hardware/Engine Simulator 2.0/Engine_Simulator_2.0_FAB_gerbers.zip` — ZIP archive containing all Gerber and drill files, ready for direct upload to the manufacturer

Board: 2 layers, 100 × 100 mm, thickness 1.6 mm, HASL finish, minimum trace width 0.2 mm, minimum clearance 0.21 mm, minimum drill 0.3 mm (via) / 2.2 mm (M2 mounting holes, PTH connected to GND).
